from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape

        {"ID": 9, "Name": "Isabella Thomas", "Course": "Biology"},
        {"ID": 10, "Name": "James Taylor", "Course": "Accounting"}

title: App1
description: Build a plain Python WSGI app using Jinja2 and Gunicorn inside a virtual environment

steps.heading: Go to Home Directory
steps.explanation: Start by navigating to your home directory.
steps.code: cd ~

steps.heading: Copy the Virtual Environment
steps.explanation: Copy the preconfigured Python virtual environment to your home directory. This must be done first before activating.
steps.code: cp -r /opt/virt ~/

steps.heading: Activate the Virtual Environment
steps.explanation: Activate the virtual environment. You should see (virt) at the start of your prompt when activated.
steps.code:
source ~/virt/bin/activate

# You should see:
# (virt) username@server:~$

steps.heading: Create webapps Directory
steps.explanation: Create and navigate into the webapps directory where your applications will live.
steps.code:
mkdir webapps
cd webapps

steps.heading: Create app1 Directory
steps.explanation: Create and navigate into the app1 directory for this specific application.
steps.code:
mkdir app1
cd app1

steps.heading: Create Empty GitHub Repository and Clone It
steps.explanation: Create an empty repository on GitHub, then clone it. The 'empty repository' warning is expected and fine.
steps.code:
git clone git@github.com:xalhexi-sch/App1.git

# You may see:
# warning: You appear to have cloned an empty repository.
# This is expected and fine.

steps.heading: Create app.py
steps.explanation: Create the main application file using nano. This is a pure WSGI app using Jinja2 for templating. Save with Ctrl+O then Enter, exit with Ctrl+X.
steps.code:
nano app.py

# Paste this code:
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader
import os

BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

env = Environment(
    loader=FileSystemLoader(os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "templates")),
    autoescape=True
)

def app(environ, start_response):
    path = environ.get("PATH_INFO", "/")

    if path.endswith("/hello"):
        title = "Hello Page"
        message = "Rendered using Jinja2"
    else:
        title = "Home"
        message = "Plain Python + Gunicorn + Nginx"

    template = env.get_template("home.html")
    html = template.render(title=title, message=message)

    start_response("200 OK", [("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")])
    return [html.encode("utf-8")]

steps.heading: Create Templates Folder and HTML File
steps.explanation: Create the templates directory and the home.html template file. This uses Jinja2 syntax with {{ variable }} placeholders.
steps.code:
mkdir templates cd templates nano home.html # Paste this HTML: {{ title }}

{{ title }}

{{ message }}

steps.heading: Return to App Root
steps.explanation: Navigate back to the app1 directory and verify your location with pwd.
steps.code:
cd ..
pwd

# Expected output:
# ~/webapps/app1

steps.heading: Run the App Using Gunicorn
steps.explanation: Start the application using Gunicorn. You can change the port (5000) if needed. The app:app refers to the app function inside app.py.
steps.code: gunicorn --bind 127.0.0.1:5000 app:app

steps.heading: Access the App
steps.explanation: Access your app through the server URL. The exact URL depends on your server/proxy setup.
steps.code:
# Example URL (depends on your server setup):
# http://172.17.100.15:9899/it21_banas/webapps/app1

# Final folder structure:

# └── app1/
#     ├── app.py
#     └── templates/
#         └── home.html

title: Git Basics: Create Repo & Push
description: Create a new repository, add files, commit changes, and push to GitHub

steps.heading: Create Project Folder
steps.explanation: Create a project folder and navigate into it. Use pwd to verify your location.
steps.code:
mkdir my-project
cd my-project

# Optional: check where you are
pwd

steps.heading: Initialize Git Repository
steps.explanation: Initialize Git in the folder and set the branch to 'main' (recommended).
steps.code:
git init

# Set branch to main
git branch -M main

steps.heading: Create Files
steps.explanation: Create a README file using nano. Save with Ctrl+O then Enter, exit with Ctrl+X. You can also create files quickly with echo.
steps.code:
# Create README with nano
nano README.md

# Or create file quickly
echo "Hello world" > hello.txt

# Check your files
ls

steps.heading: Check Status & Stage Files
steps.explanation: Check Git status to see untracked files, then add them to staging area.
steps.code:
git status

# Add all files
git add .

# Or add specific file
git add README.md

# Check status again
git status

steps.heading: Commit Changes
steps.explanation: Commit your staged changes with a descriptive message.
steps.code: git commit -m "Initial commit"

steps.heading: Create GitHub Repo & Connect
steps.explanation: On GitHub: Click 'New repository', name it, do NOT initialize with README. Copy the SSH link and connect your local repo.
steps.code:
# Add remote (replace USERNAME and my-project)
git remote add origin git@github.com:USERNAME/my-project.git

# Verify remote
git remote -v

steps.heading: Push to GitHub
steps.explanation: Push your commits to GitHub. The -u flag sets upstream, so future pushes only need 'git push'.
steps.code:
git push -u origin main

# Future pushes:
git push

steps.heading: Normal Workflow
steps.explanation: After initial setup, use this workflow when you make changes: status, add, commit, push.
steps.code:
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Describe what you changed"
git push

title: Ubuntu: Rename & Move Files
description: How to rename files and move them between folders in Ubuntu

steps.heading: Rename a File
steps.explanation: Use mv command to rename files. Same syntax works for folders.
steps.code:
# Rename a file
mv oldname.txt newname.txt

# Example
mv notes.txt notes-final.txt

# Rename a folder
mv oldfolder newfolder

steps.heading: Move File to Parent Folder
steps.explanation: Use ../ to reference the parent folder. Move files one level up with mv.
steps.code:
# Move file one level up
mv file.txt ../

# Move folder one level up
mv myfolder ../

# Move multiple files up
mv a.txt b.txt c.txt ../

steps.heading: Move Multiple Levels Up
steps.explanation: Use multiple ../ to go up several levels. Each ../ goes up one folder.
steps.code:
# ../ = up 1 folder
# ../../ = up 2 folders
# ../../../ = up 3 folders

# Move file up 2 levels
mv file.txt ../../

steps.heading: Move File Into Another Folder
steps.explanation: Move a file into a subfolder by specifying the folder name.
steps.code:
mv file.txt foldername/

# Example
mv hello.txt src/

steps.heading: Check Location & List Files
steps.explanation: Helpful commands to see where you are and what files exist.
steps.code:
# Print working directory
pwd

# List files
ls

# List all files with details
ls -la

steps.heading: Common mistakes that caused problems before
steps.code:
## Wrong `remote` URL in `/etc/pterodactyl/config.yml`

Bad:
remote: http://panel.cookie-hosting.com

Good:
remote: https://panel.cookie-hosting.com

## Wrong daemon port in panel

Bad:
Daemon Port: 443

Good:
Daemon Port: 8080

## Trying to use raw IP forever

Possible, but messy. Real subdomain + SSL is cleaner and worked better.

## Cloudflare proxied

Bad for this use:
Proxy status: Proxied

Good:
Proxy status: DNS only

## Certbot timeout

Usually means:
* port 80 blocked in UFW
* port 80 blocked in provider firewall
* DNS not pointed correctly
* Cloudflare proxied

Project Title:
Integrated Classroom Maintenance and Equipment Management System for the PMO Department at Father Saturnino Urios University (F.S.U.U.)

JOHN JIV H. VIVARES

ROMMEL D. CONQUILLA
________________________________________
1. Introduction
In educational institutions like Father Saturnino Urios University (F.S.U.U.), maintaining classrooms and managing equipment efficiently is essential to ensure a conducive learning environment. Damaged furniture, broken equipment, and unavailable resources can disrupt academic activities and affect both teaching and learning processes.
Currently, maintenance concerns and equipment requests are handled manually or through informal communication, which often results in delays, miscommunication, and lack of proper tracking. There is also no centralized system that allows users to monitor equipment availability in real time.
To address these issues, this project proposes the development of an Integrated Classroom Maintenance and Equipment Management System for the PMO department. The system will digitalize reporting, tracking, borrowing, and inventory management while ensuring secure and role-based access for all users.
________________________________________
2. Statement of the Problem
The current process of handling maintenance and equipment management presents several challenges:
1.	Lack of a centralized system for reporting issues 
2.	Difficulty in tracking maintenance requests and equipment status 
3.	Inefficient monitoring of borrowed and returned equipment 
4.	Limited visibility of available equipment for users 
5.	Poor record-keeping and report generation 
6.	Lack of accountability due to absence of user tracking 
________________________________________
3. Objectives
General Objective:
To design and develop an integrated system that manages classroom maintenance, equipment inventory, and borrowing processes for the PMO department of F.S.U.U.
Specific Objectives:
1.	To implement a secure login system with role-based access 
2.	To provide separate dashboards for admin and users 
3.	To create a centralized monitoring dashboard 
4.	To manage users and staff accounts efficiently 
5.	To maintain and update equipment inventory 
6.	To allow users to view real-time equipment availability 
7.	To track borrowing and returning of equipment 
8.	To monitor maintenance requests and repair history 
9.	To manage classroom assignments and equipment distribution 
10.	To support procurement and acquisition processes 
11.	To generate accurate and detailed reports 
________________________________________
4. Conceptual Framework
The system follows the Input–Process–Output (IPO) Model, integrating multiple modules for efficient PMO operations.
 
•	User login credentials 
•	Maintenance requests 
•	Equipment and inventory data 
•	Borrowing and return records 
•	Procurement requests 
________________________________________
Process:
A. Authentication & Access Control
•	Secure login and logout 
•	Role-based authentication (Admin vs Users) 
•	Automatic redirection to separate dashboards 
B. Dashboard Module
•	Displays system overview 
•	Shows statistics (equipment, users, borrow records) 
C. User & Staff Management Module
•	Add, edit, delete users 
•	Assign roles and permissions 
D. Inventory / Equipment Management Module
•	Manage equipment records 
•	Track availability 
•	Provide real-time availability view 
E. Borrowing System Module
•	Track borrowed and returned items 
F. Maintenance Management Module
•	Log and monitor repairs 
G. Classroom Management Module
________________________________________
5. Scope and Limitations
Scope:
•	Includes students, teaching staff, non-teaching staff, and PMO staff 
•	Provides separate dashboards for Admin and Users 
Users can:
•	Submit requests 
•	Borrow equipment 
•	Track status 
•	View equipment availability 
PMO Admin can:
•	Control entire system 
•	Manage all records 
________________________________________
Limitations:
•	Restricted access per role 
•	Requires internet 
•	Limited to PMO functions 
________________________________________
6. System Design Overview
•	Role-based login system 
•	Separate Admin and User dashboards 
•	Secure and efficient workflow 
________________________________________
7. Methodology
SDLC Approach:
Planning → Analysis → Design → Implementation → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance
________________________________________
8. Expected Output
•	Functional system 
•	Real-time tracking 
•	Organized records 
________________________________________
9. Conclusion
The system improves PMO operations through automation, real-time tracking, and secure access. It ensures efficiency, accountability, and better campus management.
